title: Terraform preflight: inventory & quota auditor for Private (VPC) installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide a deterministic, actionable Terraform/IaC preflight auditor that runs before Private (VPC) installs to validate cloud quotas, IAM configuration, DNS & networking preconditions, and GPU provisioning capacity. The auditor must be usable as (1) a Terraform plan/post-plan hook, (2) a CI step, and (3) a standalone CLI for SREs/SEs doing customer onboarding. This ticket scopes the spec, implementation plan, and an initial PoC module + CI integration.

Background: We've had several onboarding delays where installs failed due to missing quotas (vCPUs, ENIs, GPUs), mis-scoped IAM roles, private DNS not created, or wrong GPU drivers/AMIs in target accounts. Current checks are ad-hoc. We need a repeatable automated check that returns a clear machine-readable report and human summary with remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight runs as a Terraform external data/plan-time step and exits non-zero when critical failures are detected

Checks include: cloud quotas (compute, vCPU, GPUs, ENIs), IAM roles & policies, KMS/S3 access for Terraform state, DNS zone records (private zone presence and delegation), subnet capacity per AZ, and GPU SKU availability in requested region/AZ
Produces a JSON report with severity (critical, warning, info) and actionable remediation steps per finding
CLI mode (rw-preflight) that can be run from CI and returns user-friendly summary in terminal and a machine-readable artifact
Module is documented with runbook steps for SE onboarding and included in the Private deployment quickstart
Smoke validation: run preflight against 3 staging accounts and a sample customer account; all known issues are detected and reported in CI
Security review completed for IAM permissions used by the auditor (least privilege principle)
tasks: Spec: enumerate checks and failure modes + define JSON schema for report
Design: Terraform module interface (inputs/outputs) + CLI UX
Implementation: PoC Go CLI and terraform null_resource/provider wrapper
Cloud provider implementation: AWS (v1) -> compute quotas, GPU SKUs, ENI limits, service quotas API calls
Integrate with CI: add preflight step to private-deployments pipeline and sample repo
Docs: runbook, remediation snippets, sample outputs
QA: run extensive tests across AZs, emulate quota-gapped accounts
proposed_solution:
Build a small reusable 'rw-infra-preflight' module and CLI that performs a layered set of checks:
1) Inventory checks: confirm Terraform state backend reachable (S3/GCS), KMS keys accessible, and required IAM roles/service accounts exist and match allowlists.
2) Quota checks: query provider service-quotas (AWS Service Quotas) and compute resource availability (vCPUs, GPUs by SKU, ENIs, public IPs). For GPUs, check for capacity insights (where supported) and fall back to soft checks (region SKU presence + historical availability metrics).
3) Network/DNS checks: confirm VPC/subnet sizing, CIDR overlaps, presence of private hosted zones and expected records (controller endpoints, bootstrap records), NAT gateway counts, route table reachability to internet endpoints required for installers.
4) Runtime checks (optional): from a supplied bastion or a transitive test container, try to pull the GPU AMI and validate driver compatibility via simple metadata checks.

The module will expose a 'critical_failures' boolean and a JSON report output. It should be pluggable into Terraform as an external/remote-exec step and usable standalone from CI with environment credentials. The PoC will target AWS first and provide an extensible adapter interface for GCP/Azure later.
implementation_notes: Use Go for CLI (binary distribution) to avoid Python dependency issues in SE environments
Leverage AWS Service Quotas + EC2 DescribeInstanceTypeOfferings + DescribeInstanceTypes to assess GPU SKU availability
Design the Terraform wrapper as an optional module that invokes the CLI via null_resource local-exec or external data source and captures JSON as output
Limit IAM permissions: read-only APIs (service-quotas:Get*, ec2:Describe*, route53:ListHostedZones, iam:GetRole, kms:DecryptMetadata), avoid making modifications
Add a dry-run mode and a '--fix-suggestions' flag that prints exact console/API steps for remediation (not automated fixes)
Record telemetry (opt-in) to help us understand common failure modes across customers (quota type, missing roles)
test_plan: Unit tests for report schema validation
Integration tests mocking quota APIs to simulate low quota and GPU-scarce regions
End-to-end run in staging accounts with telemetry enabled and assertions on expected failures
Run against 3 recent customer accounts (with consent) to verify detectability of past failures
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Service Quotas APIs have eventual consistency; a quota increase request might not be visible immediately. Mitigation: mark those as warnings and include timestamp checks and guidance to re-run after quota ops complete.

Risk: GPU availability is not strictly queryable in all clouds; mitigation: combine SKU presence checks with regional historical signals and add an explicit opt-in manual probe that hits the marketplace/AMI if allowed.
Risk: Over-privileged preflight roles. Mitigation: run security review, require least-privilege policy and audit logs for preflight runs.
Risk: False positives blocking installs. Mitigation: tier findings (critical vs warning) and allow operator override via 'allow-warnings' flag in automation with explicit sign-off
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge PoC CLI + Terraform wrapper to feature branch; run in staging pipelines
Week 2: Iterate based on staging results, fix gaps for common quota types (ENIs, IPv4 addresses), add improved messaging
Week 3: Run limited beta with 2 SE-led customer onboards; collect feedback
Week 4: GA: publish module to internal registry, add to private-deployments quickstart and CI template
